identificationModule.officialTitle: Peri- Versus Intra-operative Anti-vascular Endothelial Growth Factor Intravitreous Injections for Diabetic Macular Edema in Patients Undergoing Cataract Surgery

statusModule.whyStopped: The study team was unable to secure sufficient funding and administrative support.

descriptionModule.briefSummary: Goals of the study are to evaluate how peri-operative versus intra-operative anti-VEGF intravitreous injections affect visual acuity (BCVA) in patients with persistent diabetic macular edema who are undergoing cataract surgery; and to evaluate how peri-operative versus intra-operative anti-VEGF intravitreous injections affect OCT CSF thickness and total number of postoperative injections in patients with diabetic macular edema who are undergoing cataract surgery.
descriptionModule.detailedDescription:
Along with age, diabetes is a major risk factor for cataract formation, which can lead to significant vision loss and disability without medical intervention. Unfortunately, diabetic patients, particularly those with diabetic macular edema (DME), experience poorer visual outcomes after undergoing cataract surgery compared to non-diabetics. Reasons for this is multifactorial but includes an increased risk in the development of post-operative cystoid macular edema, and exacerbation of baseline DME. This poses a significant challenge in managing concomitant DME and visually-significant cataracts.

Goals of the study are to evaluate how peri-operative versus intra-operative anti-VEGF intravitreous injections affect visual acuity (BCVA) in patients with persistent diabetic macular edema who are undergoing cataract surgery; and to evaluate how peri-operative versus intra-operative anti-VEGF intravitreous injections affect OCT CSF thickness and total number of postoperative injections in patients with diabetic macular edema who are undergoing cataract surgery.

armGroups.label: Aflibercept injected Pre- and Post-operatively
armGroups.description: Pre- and Post-operative time of Aflibercept injections
interventionNames: Drug: Aflibercept injected Pre- and Post-operatively

interventions.name: Aflibercept injected Pre- and Post-operatively
interventions.description: Three injections of aflibercept before cataract surgery, and aflibercept injections after surgery within 14-21 days of the day of surgery (number of injections depends on clinical exam findings, visual acuity and retinal thickness).

interventions.name: Aflibercept injected intraoperatively
interventions.description: Three injections of aflibercept before surgery and one injection of aflibercept during the course of the surgery by cataract surgeon.

primaryOutcomes.description: BCVA is a measurement of the best vision correction that can be achieved, such as glasses, as measured on the standard Snellen eye chart. For example, if uncorrected eyesight is 20/200, but patient can see 20/20 with glasses, the BCVA is 20/20.
primaryOutcomes.timeFrame: 1 month, 3 months and 6 months after cataract surgery

secondaryOutcomes.measure: Change in optical coherence tomography (OCT) central subfield (CSF) thickness
secondaryOutcomes.description: Optical coherence tomography (OCT) is an important imaging modality in the evaluation and management of retinal diseases. Change in central subfield (CSF) thickness will be measured and recorded.
secondaryOutcomes.timeFrame: 24 hours post-operatively, 1 month, 3 months and 6 months after cataract surgery

secondaryOutcomes.description: Total number of postoperative injections will be calculated

eligibilityModule.eligibilityCriteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Adults over age 18 with diabetes mellitus, diabetic macular edema and visually significant cataracts planning to undergo cataract surgery

Exclusion Criteria:

* Patients who have undergone panretinal photocoagulation (PRP) in prior 4 months or an ocular condition (other than cataract and DME) that might affect visual acuity during course of study.
* Patients with history of vitrectomy.
* Patients with neovascular glaucoma.
